What the ranking shows

Dhan tops the delivery ranking with published zero brokerage across segments. A cluster of flat-fee brokers - Fyers, Pocketful, Arrow, Shoonya (Finvasia), Zerodha - also charge nothing on delivery while capping intraday and F&O at ₹20 or less per order. The remaining flat-fee brokers charge up to ₹20 on delivery too. For the plan-based brokers, cost depends entirely on the plan you pick and your volumes, which is why they sit outside the ranking rather than inside it with a guessed number.

Charges beyond brokerage

Brokerage is only one line on a contract note. Every trade also carries securities transaction tax, exchange transaction charges, SEBI turnover fees, GST, and stamp duty; accounts may carry AMC, and services like call-and-trade, physical statements or payment gateways can cost extra. On a delivery trade at a zero-brokerage broker, statutory charges are effectively your entire cost - identical no matter which broker you use.

Conclusion

For pure cost, the published record is unambiguous: zero-brokerage and free-delivery flat-fee brokers win, and among them the differences come down to AMC, API pricing and platform preference rather than brokerage. Confirm the current schedule on the official page before opening an account - pricing changes are frequent and rarely announced loudly.

Frequently asked questions

Which broker has the lowest brokerage in India?

On published headline pricing, Dhan is the cheapest, advertising zero brokerage across segments - statutory charges still apply. Several brokers (Zerodha, Dhan, Fyers) offer free equity delivery with flat ₹20-or-lower derivatives pricing. Brokers with plan-based pricing cannot be ranked on a single number and are listed separately.

Is zero brokerage really free trading?

No. Zero brokerage means the broker charges no commission, but every trade still incurs statutory and exchange charges - STT/CTT, exchange transaction fees, SEBI fees, GST and stamp duty. Zero-brokerage brokers earn revenue from other sources such as float income and value-added services.

Why are some brokers not ranked on this page?

Brokers with plan-based or variable pricing (for example bank-backed full-service brokers) do not publish a single flat figure that can be fairly compared with flat-fee brokers, so they are listed separately with links to their official rate cards rather than being forced into the ranking.

Do lower charges mean a better broker?

Not necessarily. Execution quality, platform stability, margin policies and support all affect real trading outcomes. For small, infrequent delivery investments, however, cost differences compound and are usually the dominant factor.
